anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 PowerPath controller U6 has VIN (pin 1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (pin 6) on +5V. Its P-channel pass FET Q1 is wired with source (Q1.2) on +5V and drain (Q1.3) on USBC_VBUS_IN, which is reversed relative to the input side.
anomalies.expected: For reverse-current protection the P-FET body diode (anode at source) must block flow from the +5V load back to the USB input. The FET source should sit on the input (USBC_VBUS_IN) and the drain on the output (+5V), matching VIN and SENSE.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: With the FET reversed, the body diode conducts from the +5V rail back into VBUS whenever the FET is off. The reverse-current protection the design is meant to provide does not work, and the 5V rail can back-feed the USB connector.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have GND2 (pin 5), the isolated-side ground, on the main GND net. No isolated ground net exists on the board. The isolated side's VCC2 is powered from 5V_switched_CAN, which is referenced to the same GND as the CM4.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes the CAN buses as isolated through an isolated CAN transceiver. The isolated-side ground (GND2) should be a separate isolated ground net, not the system GND.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
5V_switched_CAN : C15.2(2,passive) C16.2(2,passive) J13.7(Pin_7,passive) J2.7(Pin_7,passive) JP8.2(B,passive) Q9.3(D,passive) U10.8(VCC2,power_in) U11.8(VCC2,power_in)
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation the design relies on is bypassed. Ground loops and common-mode faults from the motor bus reach the CM4 ground, which defeats the purpose of the isolated transceivers.

anomalies.observed: Current-limit resistor R13 is 27R in series with green LED D12 (KT-0805G) from +3V3, with the LED cathode driven by U18.Y. At 3.3 V and a typical green forward drop of about 2.1 V, this gives roughly 40 mA.
anomalies.expected: A value around 56R to 100R, as used for the other indicator at R15 (56R, D17), keeps the current near 20 mA, within the LED's rating.

evidence.quote: D12 | LED_GREEN | LED_SMD:LED_0805_2012Metric | Device:LED | Light emitting diode | MPN= KT-0805G

anomalies.impact: The indicator LED is over-driven, which shortens its life and can overheat the 0805 part. The LED is not intended to be an overcurrent load.

parsed.summary: The most credible anomaly is the reversed P-FET (Q1) in the LTC4412 USB OR-ing path, which defeats the reverse-current protection the design is meant to provide. A secondary concern is that the isolated CAN transceivers' GND2 pins are tied to the main GND, which bypasses isolation. Confidence is moderate because some of this may be an original design choice rather than an injected fault.
